I'm 64 years old and I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years. I know every corner of my 10.1 mu. My father farmed before me, and I've learned what works here on the North China Plain. I don't have much schooling, but I have experience — and that's what counts.

This year, like every year, I'll split my land between winter wheat and summer maize. The wheat-maize rotation is the only sensible system here. I'll plant about 5.1 mu with wheat in the autumn and 5.0 mu with maize in the summer, right after the wheat comes off. I have a well, so when the rains don't come, I can irrigate — and on this plain, you often need to.

For the wheat, I'll use an improved variety. The hybrid seeds cost too much and I've had good results with the improved seeds from the local supply shop. I'll plough the land before sowing — I've always done it this way, and it prepares a good seedbed. I'll put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 5 kg of potassium. I'll irrigate three times: once after sowing to help germination, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. Too much water and you waste money and risk disease. I'll spray pesticides twice if the aphids or rust show up, which they usually do. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather cooperates.

For the maize, I'll sow hybrid seeds right after wheat harvest in June — there's no time to waste with only 5.0 mu, and hybrid maize gives the best yield in our short summer. I'll do light rotary tillage or no-tillage to save time and keep moisture. Maize needs nitrogen — about 16 kg per mu — and I'll add 5 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I'll irrigate twice: at the V6 stage and at tasseling/silking. That's enough if the summer rains are normal. One pesticide application should handle the corn borer. I expect around 600 kg per mu from the maize.

I've farmed long enough to know not to chase every new technique. I stick with what works, what my well can support, and what my family can manage on 10 mu.
